# Retro Hex Chat

> A self-hosted chat server styled after Windows 98 and mIRC. Channels, virtual
> spaces, private peer-to-peer calls over WebRTC, channel conferences, bots, and
> retro games — all in the browser. Open source under the MIT licence, built with
> Elixir, Phoenix LiveView and PostgreSQL.

The point of the project is that the server is yours. Messages live in your own
PostgreSQL database, private one-to-one calls go browser-to-browser without the
media passing through the server, and the whole thing is MIT licensed so you can
read, change and run it yourself.

The site is published in fourteen languages. English lives at the unprefixed
path and every other language under a BCP 47 segment — `/pt-BR/features`,
`/zh-Hans/faq`. Each page declares its own canonical URL and a reciprocal
`hreflang` set, so any one of them is a fine place to start.

## Start here

- [Home](https://retrohexchat.app/): what the project is and who it is for.
- [How it works](https://retrohexchat.app/how-it-works): the server, spaces,
  calls and the privacy model, with the P2P and TURN fallback explained.
- [Features](https://retrohexchat.app/features): channels, spaces, conferences,
  bots, multiplayer games and the solo arcade.
- [Games](https://retrohexchat.app/games): every game in the browser — DOOM,
  Quake, Wolfenstein 3D, Half-Life: Uplink, ScummVM adventures and multiplayer
  arcade games — each with a page and a screenshot.
- [Spaces](https://retrohexchat.app/spaces): the pixel-art world every channel
  opens onto — the island, the Construct to build in, the Game Room, the Office
  and the character creator — in pictures from the real thing.
- [Hex Paint](https://retrohexchat.app/paint): a pixel drawing program on the
  chat's desktop — sixteen retro colours, pencil, shapes and fill — whose
  drawings are posted to a channel as pictures.
- [ASCII Art](https://retrohexchat.app/ascii-art): text banners, pictures and
  pixel drawings turned into art in mIRC colours, posted as one message.
- [Hex Radio](https://retrohexchat.app/radio): an internet radio player on the
  chat's desktop — stations from around the world by genre or by name, a
  spectrum, an oscilloscope and a ten-band equalizer.
- [FAQ](https://retrohexchat.app/faq): fourteen questions on P2P, self-hosting,
  server requirements, security and contributing.

## Coming from mIRC or IRC

It is a chat in the style of mIRC that runs in the browser — not an IRC server:
IRC clients cannot connect to it.

- [mIRC commands](https://retrohexchat.app/mirc-commands): the commands mIRC
  users type most, each marked as the same here, different, or missing, with
  what to type instead.
- [mIRC online](https://retrohexchat.app/mirc-online): what of mIRC carries over
  to the browser, and what does not.
- [IRC chat](https://retrohexchat.app/irc-chat): how channels, operators, modes,
  and NickServ and ChanServ work here.

## Documentation

- [Help](https://retrohexchat.app/chat/help): roughly three hundred topics
  covering every command, channel mode, keyboard shortcut and window, each at
  its own URL and translated into all fourteen languages.
- [Component showcase](https://retrohexchat.app/showcase): the Windows 98 UI
  primitives the interface is built from, one page per component.

## Running it yourself

- [Install](https://retrohexchat.app/install): clone, set up, run — and the
  system requirements.
- [Privacy comparison](https://retrohexchat.app/privacy): data ownership, call
  routing, message access and AI training, next to the closed alternatives.
- [Community](https://retrohexchat.app/community): the licence, how to
  contribute, and where the source lives.

## Notes

- `/sitemap.xml` indexes every public URL, including each help topic in every
  language.
  Nothing said before that is ever published, and turning the switch off
  unpublishes the pages rather than leaving them up.
